paper_metadata.title: Creep deformation and damage tolerance of P/M superalloys with Ta addition

evidence.quote: tantalum (Ta) emerges as a promising additive for the development of next-generation Ni-base powder metallurgy (PM) superalloys.
This study investigates the creep rupture behavior of P/M superalloys with varying Ta content, with a focus on microstructural degradation and potential damage mechanisms.

evidence.section: 3.4 Degradation of the interfaces and strengthening phases
evidence.quote: the σ phase precipitated at the grain boundaries of Ta-containing alloys after the creep at 800 ◦C
it is important to control Mo and Cr the σ phase precipitation at the grain boundaries, because this is the main reason for the creep damage in high-Ta alloys.
it promotes the splitting of the secondary γ′ precipitate, which dynamically changes the width of the channel during creep and increases the γ′ interface.

the isolated microtwin is found in the without Ta or low-Ta alloys after 800°C/400 MPa, which indicates that the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the γ-matrix may be increased at this temperature, resulting in difficulties for leading dislocations of the isolated microtwins to cut into the matrix, allowing for fewer extended microtwin shear events.

evidence.section: 3.3 Deformed microstructures in various creep conditions
evidence.quote: Twinning is the main deformation mechanism after creep at such high stress

Microtwinning deformation is predictable at such high stresses. Therefore, it is assumed that the microtwinning is the main creep mechanism, the energy of the nearest-neighbor violation in particles can affects the creep rate.

evidence.section: 3.4 Degradation of the interfaces and strengthening phases
evidence.quote: The EPMA maps near the grain boundaries revealed that the segregation of Cr and Mo along the interfaces as well as the depletion of Ta and Ti.

evidence.section: 3.3 Deformed microstructures in various creep conditions
evidence.quote: The presence of subgrain near grain boundaries suggests that polycrystalline superalloys need to consider recovery softening during creep at 750 ◦C.
at 800°C/400 MPa, the main creep mechanism is the climbing of a/2<110> dislocations and the dissociation of dislocations to form faults due to the increase in temperature and the decrease in stress.
